Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:117421
Court No. - 93

Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 406 of 2021
Revisionist :- Ram Bahadur

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Revisionist :- Bratendra Singh,Akhilesh Srivastava,Arvind Kumar Srivastava,A
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1. Heard Sri Devendra Mohan Singh, learned counsel for the revisionist and learned A.G.A. for the
State assisted by Sri Vinay Kumar Singh, Brief-holder
and perused the record.

2.  By means of this criminal revision, the revisionist-convict has challenged the order dated 10.02.2020 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court No. 1, Rampur in criminal complaint no. 1758 of 2006 (State of U.P. vs. Ram Bahadur) by which the revisionist was convicted and sentenced for an offence under Section 7 read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) and 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 as well as order dated 25.01.2021 passed by learned Additional Session Judge, Court No. 2, Rampur in criminal appeal no. 11 of 2020 (Ram Bahadur vs.
State of U.P.), by which the judgment and order of the trial court was affirmed.
3. The revisionist on his own volition has decided to not to contest this revision on the legal grounds as mentioned in revision memo and instead he desires to confine its arguments on the basis of proviso to Section 16(1)(g) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, which is as below:-
"Provided that?
Ram Bahadur vs State Of U.P. on 25 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198226237/
1 (i) if the offence is under sub-clause (i) of clause (a) and is with respect to an article of food, being primary food, which is adulterated due to human agency or is with respect to an article of food which is misbranded within the meaning of sub-clause (k) of clause (ix) of section 2; or (ii) if the offence is under sub-clause (ii) of clause (a), but not being an offence with respect to the contravention of any rule made under clause (a) or clause (g) of sub-section (1A) of section 23 or under clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 24, the court may, for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment,
impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months but which may extend to two years, and with fine which shall not be less than five hundred rupees:"

sentences.text: 4. It is argued on the basis of above provision of law that the article of food, the subject matter of this case is milk, which comes in the category of primary food; the court has been empowered to impose a sentence of imprisonment of minimum three months and maximum two years in case a primary food is found adulterated by human agency; no objection has been raised on this issue.

5. It is brought to my notice that this case pertains to sampling, which was done in 2006; the litigation lingered on and was decided in the year 2020; the appeal filed on behalf of the convict came to be dismissed by the appellate court in the year 2021.

6. My attention has further been drawn by the learned AGA to all the contentions raised in the revision as regard compliance of the mandatory statutory provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
It is argued that all the pleas raised by the revisionist were dealt with by the trial court as well as the appellate court.

The contention as regard the compliance of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was specifically dealt with by the trial court as well as the appellate court and it was found that the notice of the same was given to the accused as per law.
In my view there is no material to show that the statutory provisions with regard to sampling and the proceeding taken thereafter suffers from any illegality.

7. Besides the contentions taken as regard the antiquity of the case, it is submitted on behalf of the revisionist that as per the prosecution case the prescribed limit for fact content in milk is 4.5% for mixed milk of cow and buffalo and as per the lab report, the fact content was found 3.5%.
It is submitted that this deficiency is minor in nature and can be caused for different reasons even without indulgence of human agency.
In my view it will not be proper for the revisional court to open up such factual aspects of the case, however this much is clear that in this case a minor deficiency of fat content was found.

8. In view of all the above reasons, in my opinion the imposing of one year of rigorous imprisonment is too harsh in the circumstances of this case, hence, while maintaining the conviction, sentence order is accordingly modified as below:-
